title: Protecting the Harvest: Farmgate Loss Pathways Linked to Food Availability
content: This chapter explores the critical role of farm-level food loss and waste (FLW) in ensuring the availability of nutritious, perishable foods. It highlights the need for effective FLW management to complement increased food production and meet global dietary needs. The chapter examines FLW pathways for fruits, vegetables, and animal-source foods (ASF), focusing on factors like production practices, harvesting methods, and postharvest handling. To reduce FLW of fruits and vegetables, it is essential to optimize harvesting approaches, including timing and handling, as well as postharvest storage to maintain quality. As food systems modernize, more stringent quality standards impact physical FLW at the farmgate, even when no food quality loss (FQL) has occurred. To reduce FLW of ASF, it is essential to optimize production systems, such as aquaculture and livestock farming, and to address specific challenges, which are all broadly linked to animal welfare, cold chain management, and hygiene practices for preserving the quality of ASF products. By implementing strategies to address these factors, we can reduce both FQL and physical FLW to increase the quantity of good quality produce that is made available to food value chains.
